blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Alluvial soil is the most widespread and fertile soil type in India, predominantly covering the Northern Plains and river valleys.
Black soil, also known as Regur soil, is highly clayey, retains moisture well, and is ideal for growing cotton.
Red soil derives its distinctive reddish color from the high diffusion of iron in crystalline and metamorphic rocks.
Laterite soil forms in regions with high temperature and heavy rainfall through intense leaching, making it rich in iron oxide and aluminum.
Saline soils (Usar soils) contain high amounts of sodium, potassium, and magnesium, rendering them infertile without chemical treatment.

blocks.content: Alluvial soils are the most extensive soil type in India, covering over forty percent of the total land area and forming the backbone of Indian agriculture.

rows: Low-lying flood plains near river beds
Higher terraces away from river banks
Higher fertility, frequently renewed by floods
Comparatively less fertile, older soil layer
Fine silt and clay, lacking nodules

items: Khadar (new alluvium) is fine-textured and fertile, whereas Bhangar (old alluvium) contains calcareous deposits known as Kankar.
Black soil exhibits a self-ploughing characteristic because it develops deep cracks upon drying and swells when wet.
Laterite soils are prominently used for cashew nut cultivation and as building bricks due to hardening upon exposure to air.
